message.content: {"summary":"Time Loop exists as a Godot 4 project at the developer artifact path with a title screen, chapter menu, 24 procedurally-defined level entries, a 30 Hz loop clock with recorded-state ghost replays, and scenario bootstrap. The current build gate passes (build-0001: import plus headless ordinary and bounded scenario launches returncode 0), and Player capture sessions ran real inputs and produced clean runtime snapshots for title, near_rewind, and near_victory. However, only three probe traces exist outside the game package, no final artwork is present (all 12 assets are mock placeholders per art-manifest), gameplay goals were never completed in any capture, and two fresh replays of the ordinary title trace diverged at frame 0. Most gameplay mechanics (ghost-held plates/doors/lasers, enemy distraction, reset clearing, exit completion and metrics, later chapters) have no runtime evidence. The deliverable is not ready.","instruction_audit":"The original instruction was audited against the Designer specification. No original requirement is missing: the Designer covers the 30-second loop, ghost replay, layering, 24 levels/4 chapters, title/menu, countdown, movement, flash/rewind, world interaction, four-loop cap, timeline, reset, completion metrics, assets/library copying, project layout, headless launch, CLI flag ordering, screenshot helper, traces, scenarios, the trace schema fields, and determinism. The core contradiction is that the instruction explicitly permits the mounted Kenney/OpenGameArt libraries and requires browsing and copying them, while the art package introduced a mock-generation path with 'libraries reported available=false' and no copied Kenney files; the Developer then used those mocks so the design's asset requirement and the 'final art' host gate are both unresolved.
